questions.short: When a people-world run ends
questions.question: When should a people-world run stop? Example: the Waltzman run of 2026-10-23 (share FQHXnP_TLKPi) ran 45 rounds at $0.2371 in all. From round 22 every concern was resolved and the decision deployed; in the 23 rounds after that the ten people only repeated moves and nothing changed. questions.blocks: how long visitors watch a run, and its cost
questions.resolves_with: This is a product call on what a finished story looks like; no test settles it.
questions.evidence: Brian, 2026-11-10: "on d1. stop condition should be configurable." Built in PR #356 (BrianMills2718/world-substrate#356): a per-world setting on the Create page, 'When to stop a run', saved with the world like 'Simulate as': stop once nothing is changing after N quiet rounds (default for new worlds, N = 6) or always run every round. scripts/run_stop.py holds the rule; scripts/run_authored_world.py records summary.stopped and the run page says why in one line. With a group decision the run stops once it is deployed or rejected and the state is back where it was N rounds earlier (the agenda churn, Q3, otherwise never stops); on the recorded c1r24 run that is round 30 of 46 (tests/test_run_stop.py). Worlds and runs saved without the setting run every round, as before.
questions.recommendation: Stop once the decision is deployed or rejected and no one's move has changed anything for 6 rounds (one operating-review period, compile_spec.py:442), and say on the page why it stopped. Costs: a late surprise after a quiet stretch would be cut off; the visitor can still choose to run more rounds.

questions.short: Petri nets or TypeDB as carrier
questions.question: Petri nets already lend World Substrate their transition semantics (docs/model/ODD.md:171; first argued in the linked-process-participants plan, retired 2026-11-09): a process is close to a transition that fires when enabled with no actor, and output arcs are close to a declared write scope. Could a typed Petri net (AlgebraicPetri) or TypeDB (relations with role players) carry the rest well enough to adopt instead of the table in scripts/build_metamodel.py: guards that read arbitrary component checks over bound participants, partial observation (who notices a firing), and refusal of an attempted move with the failed check named?

If either holds checks as guards, per-actor noticing and named refusal, adopt it as the carrier for those types; if one of the three has no counterpart, keep the own types and compose (Petri semantics for firing, own types for checks, noticing and refusal).
questions.evidence: Settled by argument: plain and typed Petri nets (AlgebraicPetri) fire a transition when its input places hold tokens, with no guard over component data; coloured Petri nets add data guards, but no Petri net models which observer notices a firing or a refusal that names its failed check; TypeDB holds typed relations with role players but runs no state-changing effects. None carries all three of guards over bound participants, per-observer noticing and named refusal, so the answer is compose: Petri semantics for firing (already lent, linked_process_participants.md:136) and the metamodel's own types for checks, noticing and refusal, which is what docs/model/METAMODEL.md records. questions.short: Is S2's fixpoint engine capability
questions.question: S2 runs immediate processes again and again inside one commit until nothing more is due (docs/plans/open_attempt.md:164, Piece 2), which changes src/world_substrate/engine.py. AGENTS.md and Decision 006 say not to add engine, scheduler, renderer or cognition capability of World Substrate's own and to host loops on Concordia or Mesa (AGENTS.md:33; roadmap/README.md:120). Does a same-moment fixpoint in engine.py count as that forbidden engine capability?
questions.blocks: slice S2 (A5, A6) and the knock-on part of the canonical run; S1 and S3 do not wait for it
questions.resolves_with: Brian's call: the rule's wording is his (Decision 006), and the earlier resolution was argued by this plan's own author, so it is not settled by agent argument. The argument for: a ramification fixpoint is a rule semantics inside the one existing transition (C+ and Event Calculus), with no new loop, clock or scheduler, bounded at 32 reactions. The argument against: it is new control flow in engine.py, and Concordia's game master or Mesa's step could host the chain instead, one reaction per step.
questions.evidence: Brian, in session 2026-10-26: "i approve", answering this question with its recommendation (allow S2 as rule semantics). Recorded as docs/decisions/009-same-moment-knock-on-effects.md; AGENTS.md, roadmap/README.md and the plan now say so.
questions.recommendation: Allow S2 as rule semantics: the fixpoint runs inside Engine.apply's existing atomic commit, adds no clock, loop or scheduler, is capped at 32 reactions with the whole moment refused on overflow, and only processes that declare timing 'immediately' use it. Hosting the chain on Concordia or Mesa steps instead would split one moment across steps, so the glass would fall in one round and break in the next, which is the behaviour Brian asked to fix.

questions.short: Seeded roll versus no randomness
questions.question: Piece 3 rolls dice from hash(run_seed, event_id), while today no rule uses randomness (docs/plans/open_attempt.md:124). Where does run_seed live, do saved worlds replay unchanged, and who gives a generated person like Sam piloting 0?
questions.blocks: S3's design, A7 and the full canonical run (A9)
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles the first two: the run loop draws run_seed once when a run starts and records it in the run record, and each roll event records its dice, so a replay reads the dice and never rolls; a world with no roll never draws, so every saved world replays unchanged (A8). The rule stays a function of state plus the recorded seed, so the invariant becomes 'no unrecorded randomness'. The third part is open: the rules writer must give people skill fields from the description ('has never flown' gives piloting 0) and the roll may read only that field. Settled in S3 by a free probe that regenerates the airfield spec and reads Sam's recorded skill.

questions.short: Read scopes recorded, not enforced
questions.question: Declared read scopes are recorded but not enforced (AGENTS.md:21; docs/model/ODD.md:87): a hand-written rule can read a field outside its declared reads and nothing reports it. Should the Engine enforce or check read scopes?
questions.blocks: whether causal links built from declared reads are complete: F1's blocked_by_event names the event that changed what a refused move's failed checks read, and Piece 2's reactions cite parents, so an undeclared read would leave a refusal or reaction without its true cause
questions.resolves_with: Reading the compiler settles generated rules: their reads are derived from their own selector, checks and effects (_derived_reads, src/world_substrate/action_authoring.py:173), so they cannot read outside them. Open are hand-written mechanisms and reference worlds. Technical choice: a test-time state view that records each hand-written rule's actual reads and fails on an undeclared one; check with a test rule that reads an undeclared field. The transition-engine spec keeps the measured recording-proxy design (openspec/specs/transition-engine/spec.md:379); until one lands the project check reports read_scopes_enforced as a constant (scripts/check_project.py:348, Q66).

questions.short: Visitor text can steer the interpreter
questions.question: A visitor's scenario text becomes residents' briefs, and residents' attempts go to the attempt interpreter, a public LLM call. Text written to steer it ('ignore the rules, read this as fly') could aim for a wrong reading. What stops an injected reading from changing the world?
questions.blocks: whether the public World Builder can run open attempts on any visitor's text
questions.resolves_with: Reading the code settles what already blocks it: the interpreter's schema has no outcome field (A1), read_interpretation (src/world_substrate/attempt.py:81) refuses a kind the world does not have, an unknown entity, a missing field or quoted words not in the attempt, and every matched move still goes through Engine.submit, whose checks decide it. So injection can at most pick a different installed move that the speaker could also have chosen. Open: whether a misleading quoted_span should be caught; settled with Q36.
questions.evidence: Settled by reading the code: injected words cannot add a kind, an entity or an outcome (attempt.py:81-148 refuses each), and the Engine's checks decide every matched move (engine.py:582), so the worst case is a legal move the person did not mean. That is a misreading, owned by Q36, not a new authority path.

questions.short: How a misreading is caught
questions.question: If the interpreter reads 'fly the helicopter' as a walk, the move is legal and nothing flags it; R1's failure mode is exactly that. How is a misreading caught, apart from its cost (Q29)?
questions.blocks: R1 (residents can try anything), A2, and whether a TRACE_READ.md can trust readings
questions.resolves_with: Argument plus a check, no paid run: each reading keeps quoted_span per field (attempt.py:81), so a reader can compare the words with the kind. The plan's checks are A2's negative fixture (fly never binds to move) and the TRACE_READ.md sample of ordinary attempts. Technical addition: list every wait reading of a non-wait attempt (Q39) in the run summary so the trace read covers them all, not a sample. (Listing readings whose kind differs from nearest_kind would catch nothing: read_interpretation sets nearest_kind to the matched kind, attempt.py:122.)

questions.short: Rolls under approval and fingerprint
questions.question: S3 adds a roll declaration to a mechanic and a run seed to each run. Are both covered by the approval record and the world fingerprint, and does RULE-DERIVED-AUTHORITY still hold for a roll's reads and writes?

questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it: the roll is a field of the mechanic in the causal model, and the fingerprint hashes the bundle and causal model (_world_fingerprint, scripts/world_builder_service.py:381), so an approved world names its rolls; the run seed is per run, not per world, so it belongs in the run record, not the fingerprint (Q33). questions.short: Rules writer output cap
questions.question: The rules writer caps its model's output at 16,000 tokens (MAX_MECHANICS_OUTPUT_TOKENS, added 2026-09-08 in 8057ff4). Brian said on 2026-10-26 that token limits are not the right way to do things. Should the cap go, and what stops OpenRouter from holding money for the model's full output allowance (the 402 seen on 2026-10-26) once it does?
questions.blocks: whether a richer generated world (more processes now that knock-on effects exist) can be cut off mid-answer by a fixed limit
questions.resolves_with: Settled by argument plus one counterexample check: read whether any saved build's rules-writer reply stopped at the cap (finish_reason length in the llm_calls table); if none did, the cap has never cut an answer and only the 402 hold matters, which is a provider-account question, not a design one.
questions.evidence: Checked 2026-10-26 in the llm_calls table (~/projects/data/llm_observability.db, read-only): all 133 world-substrate-mechanic-authoring calls (2026-10-06 to 2026-10-25) and all 153 world-substrate-rule-writer calls that recorded a finish reason ended with stop, none with length (1 mechanic-authoring and 2 rule-writer calls recorded no finish reason), so the cap has never cut an answer off. Its only effect is to lower what OpenRouter holds per call (the 2026-10-26 402 was a hold for 65,536 tokens on a key whose balance could not cover that hold). So it stays for now as a hold limit, not a size limit, and goes once the key carries enough that a full-allowance hold never fails; nothing in S2 depends on it.

questions.short: Laws that are not simple totals
questions.question: The law language in the declared-laws plan covers two shapes: a resource whose total only named moves may change (a weighted sum that stays constant, a Petri-net P-invariant), and a move meaning that pairs two effects in one move (goods one way, payment the other). Some worlds have rules that are not totals: a price set by a formula, a share of a stock, a flag that flips. Do any of the logged incidents need a law of another shape, and what happens to such rules?
questions.blocks: whether S1's law language is enough for the incidents the plan claims to fix, or grows special cases (the risk the prior-art review named)
questions.resolves_with: One counterexample check, by reading: go through each logged incident (pencil2, 4, 7, 12, 13, 14; airfield #254) and say which law shape would have caught it. If every one is a total or a pairing, S1 keeps the two shapes; a rule of another shape stays an ordinary rule that the independent review (S3) reads against the description, not a law.
questions.evidence: Read 2026-10-28 against the incident table in docs/plans/declared_laws.md (Incidents), rebuilt per build check from the incident each check's docstring names (scripts/world_builder_service.py:922-1272) and its saved world. Bookkeeping incidents are totals or pairings: restock-production-inputs (c4-run14), pack-pencils making nothing (4VmgkXIVWn4p, evidence/vanishing-goods/pencil3-share.json), a second graphite source (c4-run20, a total only if the designer names one source) and buy-boxed-pencils paying nothing (pencil13). The counterexamples are reachability, not laws: inputs nobody makes (pencil2), stock with nowhere to go (pencil4 iMrL2U84cLCS), a seller that never receives what it sells (pencil9) and demand that only grows (cafe eFmPomcnsyQq) leave every total unchanged, so no law refuses them; they go to reports of what the test run saw and to the review. A missing component (pencil4) is structure and a malformed path (pencil14) is refused by the installer. So S1 keeps two law shapes and laws claim only the bookkeeping rows; S5's four descriptions are read for another counterexample before S4 retires anything.

questions.short: Which model reviews the rules
questions.question: The independent rules review must not be the rules writer marking its own work: research finds a model rates its own output too kindly and fixes little without outside feedback. Which model and context should the review use, and is it worth its cost and time?
questions.blocks: S3's reviewer design, and whether S4 may retire any heuristic check on the strength of the review
questions.resolves_with: Prior art settles the shape (Huang et al. 2023, arXiv 2310.01798; Wataoka et al. 2024, arXiv 2410.21819): a different model family from the rules writer, a fresh context holding only the description, the declared laws and the compiled rules, and output as a list of findings (rule, quoted description words, what is wrong), never a verdict. Whether it earns its place is empirical, so one measurement, named for one decision (S4): run it on the saved worlds of every logged incident (free replays plus one review call each, a few cents) and count which incidents it names.
questions.evidence: Settled by the named measurement 2026-10-28: evidence/declared-laws/s3-review-choice/README.md (21 calls, 0 errors, $0.4356) ran three models on seven saved incident worlds; gemini-3.1-pro-preview named 7 of 9 known bugs including pencil13's unpaid purchase, deepseek 4, the same-family control 6. scripts/review_rules.py:92 uses gemini on a fresh context of description, laws and rules. Since 2026-10-30 people worlds get the same review (scripts/world_builder_service.py, _generate_people_world).

questions.short: Which heuristic checks retire
questions.question: The build runs about fourteen hand-written checks, each added after one bad world (dead-end stock, goods from nothing, a second source, vanishing moves, unanswered demand, starved holders, unsourced inputs and others in scripts/world_builder_service.py:922-1272), and some raise false alarms (the customer false alarm, pencil12 and 13). Which ones do declared laws and the review replace, and which stay?
questions.blocks: S4: which checks are removed, and so whether validation stops growing one check per bug
questions.resolves_with: Part argument, part the Q44 measurement. Argument: checks that report what the scripted test run actually saw (idle or stalled people, circling, moves never possible, people never together, refusals at the start) are observations of a real run, not guesses, so they stay. Checks that guess at bookkeeping from the rules' shape (conjuring processes, vanishing moves, second sources) retire one by one, each only when the saved world of its incident (docs/plans/declared_laws.md, Incidents) is refused by a declared law. Checks that guess at reachability (unsourced inputs, starved holders, unanswered demand, dead-end stock) cannot be replaced by laws (Q43); each becomes a report of what the test run saw (a move never possible, a field that only grew), which stays, or retires only when the review names its incident on the saved world. The missing-component check is a structural fact and stays. Moving processes retire only if the review names c4-run16's shape. Progress 2026-10-30: the people-world change (scripts/people_world.py:298) asks people worlds for laws and sends their rules to the review too. One live people-world build has run since (evidence/declared-laws/s4-waltzman-2/TRACE_READ.md:5): it declared no laws, which fits that world, and its review was skipped; #317 fixed the skip, and the next live people-world build (evidence/declared-laws/s4-waltzman-3/TRACE_READ.md:3, 2026-11-04) exercised it: the designer again declared no laws (llm-calls id 23037 returned empty resources and laws) and the review ran (id 23042) with two findings, one of them that decision-postponed-at-deadline starts with max_postponements 0 so the decision can never be delayed; the build kept those rules without a rewrite (Q55). Laws can be dropped or left out (Q49), no check has been retired yet, and the retirement table is still owed.

questions.short: Refuse at run time or check at build time first
questions.question: A declared law can be enforced when a move runs (the engine refuses a breach) or checked before any run (read each rule's effects and prove it cannot break a total). Which comes first?
questions.blocks: S2's scope
questions.resolves_with: An argument settles it. The run-time check is the guarantee for every step that runs: it holds for every rule shape, and the build's scripted test run already runs the rules, so a breach there is a build finding for free. It does not see steps the test run never plays; a breach of those shows later as a refusal in live play, named by its law, which is safe but late. A static proof is sound only for add and subtract effects with fixed amounts, so it is an optional speed-up, not the guarantee.
questions.evidence: Settled by argument 2026-10-28: S2 builds the run-time law check inside Engine.apply's commit, beside the write-scope check (src/world_substrate/engine.py:705), and inside each knock-on wave; a law breach in the test run becomes a build finding sent to the rules writer. The static check is deferred and needs no decision now.

questions.short: One resource under several field names
questions.question: In pencil13 the customer paid from customer.cash into the shop's business.cash: the same money sits under different component names on different entities. A law that names one {component, field} cannot say that both are cash. How does a law name a resource?
questions.blocks: S1's law contract: whether the pencil13 pairing and the cash total can be written at all
questions.resolves_with: Read the incident: the pencil13 trace audit shows #277 had to match payment by last field name, a guess. The designer knows which fields hold the same thing, so the law should say so: a resource is declared once with every place it is kept ({resource_id, says, kept_in: [{component, field}, ...]}), a total sums all those places over all holders, and a pairing's gives and pays name resource ids, not fields.
questions.evidence: Settled by reading 2026-10-28: evidence/pencil13-trace-audit/TRACE_READ.md:24-25 records customer.cash paying into business.cash and the last-field-name match added in #277. docs/plans/declared_laws.md Piece 1 now declares resources with every field they are kept in, and laws name resources.

questions.short: A law that allows too much
questions.question: The designer may declare a law that is wrong for the world. Too narrow (a total that omits a move the description needs) shows up as a refusal and the review names it; that half is settled. Too permissive (a total that lets a move create cash the description says it cannot, or a pairing on a move that is a gift) breaks nothing at run time. What catches a law that allows too much?
questions.blocks: S4: whether a heuristic check whose incident is a conjured good may retire on the strength of a declared total law, when that law might itself list the conjuring move
questions.resolves_with: Argument: a permissive law is model output read by the same outside reviewer, which is asked about moves that conjure or destroy a good the description says comes from somewhere (prompts/rules_reviewer.yaml:35). So S4 retires a conjuring check only when the review names the conjuring move on the incident's saved world, not when a law merely exists. That rule is the answer; it stays open until S4 applies it to the conjuring checks' saved worlds, and reopens if the review misses a permissive law on one of them.
questions.evidence: Too-narrow half settled 2026-10-30: evidence/declared-laws/s3-review-choice/README.md:20 (gemini on pencil-s2-2: "the cedar law does not name this move and would refuse it"); prompts/rules_reviewer.yaml:37 asks about laws naming too few moves; ODD 8.22 (docs/model/ODD.md:275) records that the review reads the laws, the decision this question first blocked.

questions.short: A law the designer leaves out
questions.question: In 5 of 9 saved pencil builds the designer declared no payment law (s1-pencil, s2-pencil-2, s2-pencil-3, s3-pencil-2 with no laws at all, and the shared s3-pencil-4 run whose 8 laws only limit which moves change a stock). A missing law refuses nothing, and the reviewer is told not to report a good for being absent from the laws. What catches a sale nobody pays for when no law covers it?
questions.blocks: S4: Q45 retires a check when its incident's saved world is refused by a declared law; with laws left out that test can pass on worlds that still have the bug. Also A1 and A4, whose expected results include a payment law.
questions.resolves_with: Argument from the runs: the review already looks for 'a purchase that moves goods but no money' (prompts/rules_reviewer.yaml:30-31) whether or not a law names it, so the catch is the review, not the law. S4 therefore retires a pairing check only when the review names the unpaid move on the incident's saved world; the s3-review-choice run shows that held for pencil13 (gemini) and failed for pencil-s2-kept (no reviewer), so the pairing checks stay until the review catches pencil-s2-kept. Asking the designer for a pairing law on every move that changes two holders' stock is the other route; it is a prompt change to try only if the review keeps missing it.

questions.short: What counts as finished
questions.question: The declared-laws plan's done_when (L1-L8) checks that its parts work, and its do_not_gate_on excludes Brian's review of a run. Nothing states when the product itself is good enough, so each paid build finds a new defect and asks for another. In Brian's words on 2026-11-03: "we just seem to be rerunning the simulation". What result ends this work?
questions.blocks: Whether the paid builds in S5, L5, A4 and A6 run now, and which defect is fixed next. Merges under the plan stay ungated by Brian's review; only new paid builds wait.
questions.resolves_with: Brian's judgement on a working run, not a test: he reads one shared Waltzman run and says what is wrong. Since 2026-11-04 a shared run recorded after #317 and #320 exists: the Waltzman rebuild at 096c129, share jyVbywXT8N8F (evidence/declared-laws/s4-waltzman-3/TRACE_READ.md:3, saved without a readout), but its rules carry a review finding the build kept (no postponement possible, Q55), and the rules are written afresh on each build (5 of 5 needed and no postponement here, 4 of 5 and one postponement in s4-waltzman-2, evidence/declared-laws/s4-waltzman-3/TRACE_READ.md:16), so it is the one to judge only once Q55 is answered or with that caveat stated beside it; the recommendation to keep one saved world and improve it is what makes builds that differ comparable. His first reaction ("this is blank and doesnt play") was answered by #328 and #329: a shared run's picture is now drawn from its recorded rounds (scripts/world_builder_home.html:913).
questions.recommendation: Finished when Brian reads one shared Waltzman run and the people behave believably and something surprising follows from their choices. Keep one saved world and improve it; his reaction to it picks the next fix.
questions.evidence: Brian, 2026-11-09: "believable is just in the cotnext of off the shelf agents if you are talking about that agents simulating people act beleivaby. trying to set a metric for this doesnt make sense and is subjective. we can fine utn that later once everythgin else runs great." So believability is the off-the-shelf people agents' job (Concordia), no metric is set for it, and it is tuned only after everything else runs well; the finish line for current work is that the rest of the system works, not a believability score. Paid builds are no longer held for a believability judgement.

questions.question: In the 2026-11-04 Waltzman rebuild Country Two reopened its own settled concern (r6-e00007) with no new evidence, only saying it should not treat the concern as settled, and that kept support below what the decision needed. Should a world's rules let a person reopen a settled concern without something new?

questions.short: What the engine gives the judge before a rule exists
questions.question: An attempt no rule covers commits no event, and propagation starts only from a committed event, so what can the engine compute for such an attempt and hand to the judge, and how is Brian's 'deliver the results of that propagation to the judge' met?
questions.blocks: J1's report, J2's call order, and A2 and A3.
questions.resolves_with: Argument from the engine code: what discover() computes without a rule, and what a dry run of a proposed rule on a copy of the world gives.
questions.evidence: Settled by argument (inferred by agent, 2026-11-09, after the cold review's finding 1). The judge works in two passes. Pass 1: the engine computes what needs no new rule, from a fixed selection: engine.discover (src/world_substrate/engine.py:380-440) for the person acting and for each person the attempt names, with each move's checks, plus the current values of the entities the attempt names. discover lists only the moves of the person asked, so the port's 'sign release: blocked, inspected is false' comes from Rosa's page, not Vik's (cold review 2 of 2026-11-09, finding 3); today's runs record a few blocked rows per resident as blocked_by_rules (scripts/run_authored_world.py:601-634), not tied to an attempt. The judge proposes a ruling written as a rule. Pass 2: the engine runs the rules check and test-runs the proposed rule on a copy of the world, giving the consequence report (net changes, blockers, chain length and stopping point); the judge confirms, revises once or withdraws; only then is the rule installed and the attempt settled through it. An attempt an installed rule covers but whose check fails is refused by the engine with no judge call (A3). Plan: docs/plans/ai_judge.md, Canonical example.

questions.short: Can the rule language express a ruling

questions.evidence: Settled by reading and 3 real rulings (2026-11-09). The language is action-mechanic/v0 (src/world_substrate/action_authoring.py); its expression kinds are literal, action field, participant, entity id, owner reference and event id (action_authoring.py:893-927), with no arithmetic between two values. The three plain-baseline rulings (evidence/ai-judge/plain-baseline/rules-check.json) went through validate_bundle and CausalModel.from_dict: the cafe rule was rejected (a field named 'from' is not an identifier), the shop rule was rejected (participants must exactly name entity_ref fields), and the sawmill rule was accepted but charges one price for 3 logs because price times quantity cannot be written. Answer: the language expresses transfers guarded by checks; it cannot multiply two values or require another person's agreement, which is routed to that person (Decided 4). A ruling the check rejects after one revision is refused with 'no rule could express this' and recorded as a language gap.

The earlier wording, where a ruling settled its own attempt with nothing installed, was an outcome with no rule and is withdrawn.
